newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon halts palmoil exports for six months.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon halts palmoil exports for six months.

text.p: Cameroon said on Wednesday that it was halting exports of palmoil so that it could guarantee supplies to the home market.
"This measure is to guarantee an unbroken supply of palmoil as we are approaching a low production period," minister of commerce Justin Ndioro said.
Cameroon is the major supplier of palmoil to five neighbouring countries, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon.
Cameroon produces around 220,000 tonnes of palmoil a year, and only 60,000 is consumed locally.

Sources close to the government said the decision was taken to suspend exports following reports that opposition parties were trying to create an artificial shortage and send prices soaring in order to whip up discontent.

A presidential election is due in October. In the months leading up to the last presidential election in October 1992, basic consumer goods were in short supply, apparently because of the activities of speculators.
Ndioro said palmoil producers had agreed only to sell to their usual customers in coming months. New would-be customers would be turned away.
